newsitem.title: UK: Channel Express to buy 3 more second-hand A30OB4s.
newsitem.headline: Channel Express to buy 3 more second-hand A30OB4s.

text.p: Channel Express, the contract service operating cargo aircraft subsidiary of the UK's Dart Group Plc, plans to own and fly a further three wide-body A300B4 freighters by 2000, its A300 programmes director Anthony St Hill said.

It purchased a former Eastern Airlines/VIASA A300B4 passenger aircraft in February. This is being wet-leased -- covering the hire of both plane and crew -- initially for one year by British Airways Plc, to operate regular London Gatwick-Tel Aviv cargo charters from February 1997, said BA's freighter manager John White.

St Hill said Channel Express planned to acquire a second A300B4 by late 1997 and two more by 2000. The aircraft acquired this year is now being converted into a freighter at Filton, near Bristol, by British Aerospace Aviation Services.

"Of some 180 of this aircraft type that are still available in passenger configuration around the world, about 20 percent are for sale. So there is no shortage of these aircraft for cargo conversion purposes," he added.
"We have been inspecting a number, although purchase negotiations have yet to begin," he said.

St Hill said the carrier now owns and operates six Fokker F27 and six Dart Herald freighters and four 15-tonne capacity all-cargo Lockheed Electras on behalf of a range of contract customers that includes United Parcel Service, Federal Express and TNT Express Worldwide

St Hill added Channel Express had looked at used trijet types such as Lockheed L10-11-500s and McDonnell Douglas DC-10-10s and DC-10-30s. However it had decided the A300B4 freighter was best suited to the needs of its customers and their European operating requirements over the next 10 to 15 years.

"Our view was that a trijet was too large, although if we ever decide to go long haul then we may have to step up to that size. But most of our integrator customers are now looking towards the A300 to take over from their present Boeing 727-size freighters," he said.

He said their preference for the A300 over their existing, smaller aircraft was its ability to meet increasingly stringent anti-noise regulations in Europe and its larger (up to 45 tonnes maximum) cargo capacity required to make the most of limited airport slot opportunities.
St Hill also said that over the next few years, Channel Express would replace all of its remaining six Dart Heralds with F27s.

"And by 2005, we are also thinking of replacing our Electras with aircraft the size of Boeing 737-300s, although at present the cost of this aircraft type is too high for us to consider undertaking cargo conversions of it," he said.
